name: crm
title: CRM
summary: Companies, contacts and deals per org with pipelines, a deals board, custom properties, tags, a timeline of activities and tasks with mentions and reminders, saved views, duplicates and merge, CSV import and export, and a dashboard; every record is shared through access; teams on HubSpot or Salesforce work their CRM here live through their own connection.
stitch: Decide the default record access for new orgs (crm_settings.record_access defaults to everyone_edits; admins change it in CRM settings) and whether members hold crm.import / crm.delete (defaults: owners and admins) in Settings → Permissions.
Place CRM in the navigation: it ships a main-nav entry and a Home tile on web and a Home entry on mobile. Move it to a mobile tab (expo-router Tabs.Screen for crm/index) if the product is CRM-first.
Link to records from other features with the app paths /crm/companies/<id>, /crm/contacts/<id> and /crm/deals/<id>; notifications and search results already use them.

Adjust the default pipeline (Qualified, Meeting booked, Proposal sent, Negotiation, Won, Lost) and the seeded custom properties to the product's sales motion; bootstrap creates the default pipeline once per org.
Review the copy of record access modes (CRM_RECORD_ACCESS in shared/format.ts) and the lifecycle stages if the team doesn't use HubSpot's terms.

If the agents feature is installed, its per-resource scopes apply to CRM records through access (crm.team and crm.workspace are their parents); nothing to wire. Without it, agents get the user's own level capped at edit.

Pick each workspace's CRM in CRM settings → Connected CRMs (app, connected or both; default app) and which platforms people may connect. Connecting accounts needs the connectors feature (2.0) with HubSpot/Salesforce OAuth apps registered for this deployment; without it the CRM works as before and offers no connected sources.
